Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. _Reviewed August 28, 2026, 9:02 PM ET / August 29, 2026, 01:02 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes The PR restores Chrome DevTools MCP page creation through the browser extension relay by admitting only the operation’s initial blank tab until it navigates or is safely cleaned up. ## Regression provenance Possible regression — probable (reproduction; reviewed change). No predecessor PR is attributed. ## Merge readiness ⚠️ **Ready for maintainer review - 3 items remain** Keep open for maintainer handling. Current main still rejects the initial blank target created by blank-first CDP clients; this branch adds a scoped extension-owned creation, attachment, and cleanup flow, with no introduced blocking defect found. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `eb8f8d8e22c26d2ba500ac78577877bc2c665f1f` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | The repair is well-covered and structurally coherent, with a material browser-access boundary still requiring maintainer acceptance. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: The PR is member-authored; its body reports real Chrome/MCP after-fix evidence, while this read-only environment could not retrieve external artifacts. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: The PR is member-authored; its body reports real Chrome/MCP after-fix evidence, while this read-only environment could not retrieve external artifacts. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 8 items | Current-main gap: Current main applies ordinary tab eligibility to the created blank tab, then separately attempts attachment; it has no operation-owned initial-blank provenance.
Current-main creation sequence: Current main creates the target and subsequently calls the separate attachment path, which explains the blank-first failure described in the linked issue.
Scoped repair owner: The branch records private creation provenance, permits only that record’s initial about:blank target, validates a pending destination independently, and limits rollback to the still-current tab identity. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The browser extension relay translates external CDP commands into authenticated Chrome extension actions. Page creation starts with a blank tab, then requires debugger attachment, navigation, and eventual target cleanup. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Chrome DevTools MCP] --> B[External CDP command] B --> C[Browser relay] C --> D[Extension tab-access owner] D --> E[Initial blank tab policy] E --> F[Debugger attach and navigation] F --> G[Target lifecycle result] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should the signed-in-browser policy admit only a relay operation’s own initial about:blank tab until navigation or cleanup completes? | **Accept the bounded design:** Accept the operation-scoped exception because provenance, destination checks, lifecycle expiry, and guarded rollback constrain it to MCP creation. | Why: The code and focused negative-path coverage support the narrow design, but accepting this browser-control boundary is a maintainer security decision rather than an automation repair task. ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - This changes which ephemeral initial document may reach Chrome debugger attachment in a signed-in profile; the exception is tightly scoped, but its access-boundary tradeoff needs explicit maintainer acceptance before merge. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - No repair work remains to automate; the remaining gate is maintainer acceptance of the browser access boundary.

### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Production versus test delta** | production +537/-155; tests/test support +961/-12; docs +13 | The bug repair adds a lifecycle owner and rollback boundary, making its substantial production growth relevant to merge review. | ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Complete scoped boundary review (recommended)** Confirm that operation-bound blank provenance and its negative-path coverage are acceptable before merging. 2. **Accept the bounded exception** Merge with explicit maintainer acceptance that this transient initial-blank admission is the intended signed-in-browser policy. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Land the owner-boundary repair after the browser/security owner accepts the transient initial-blank exception and exact-head gates remain green. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes. The linked issue supplies a concrete blank-first Chrome DevTools MCP flow, and the branch exercises create, navigate, inspect, detach, and close through the relay and extension policy. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes. Keeping provenance, grouping, attachment, and rollback in the extension tab-access owner avoids a global blank allowlist or client-specific workaround. Public docs: [`docs/tools/chrome-extension.md`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/chrome-extension). ([`docs/tools/chrome-extension.md:122`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/chrome-extension), [eb8f8d8e22c2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/eb8f8d8e22c2)) Likely related people: - **steipete:** Merged the external CDP and all-tabs access work that owns the affected browser relay and tab-access paths. (role: feature owner; confidence: high; commits: [d6801f23d4e5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d6801f23d4e5f42793bd330495750f396a867ecd), [8362f74c995b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8362f74c995b0cad040303394e70f54da78ef733); files: `extensions/browser/chrome-extension/modules/tab-access.js`, `extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay/relay-bridge.ts`) - **Piyush Bag:** Recent continuity work in the browser relay area is attributable to commit 91888cf68bcac293a56b942074da0621546401f1. The owning Chrome-extension directory, extension-relay directory, and changed browser documentation have no intervening changes. The reviewer’s unavailable promisor/network objects are not a gap in the lead’s source comparison.
- **Chrome/dependency contract checked directly:** installed MCP 1.8.0 creates a page before navigation; bundled Puppeteer 25.8.0 sends `Target.createTarget` with `about:blank`. The actual Chrome creation snapshot was `url: ""`, `pendingUrl: "about:blank"`, not an already committed page. [Chrome Tabs API](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/tabs) and installed source were inspected. Only the policy’s exact newly created tab receives private transient provenance; an existing/manual blank cannot obtain it from grouping, snapshots, pause/regrant, restart, or a copied client identifier. Restricted pending destinations still fail the normal eligibility checks. MCP’s observed detach-before-close sequence is why target identity must outlive its debugger session.
- **Owner decision and best fix:** this proceeds under @steipete’s explicit fix/test/land direction for the browser-owner repair, preserving the originally required restricted/paused/sharing boundaries. It is not being represented as a separate human review approval. Creation/rollback belongs to the extension policy, document freshness is distinct from tab-access revocation, and debugger-session lifetime is distinct from target identity. Broadly admitting blanks, substituting a client-specific URL, dependency patches, and consumer-only guards were rejected. The +382 production LOC pays for those missing ownership boundaries; the split creator/grouping implementation and redundant modern attachment path were removed. No new configuration, permission, schema, budget, or suppression.

Local proof on the refreshed commit: 328 owner/sibling tests pass; the complete canonical build passes (345,187 startup gzip bytes / 345,947-byte limit); actual isolated MCP, Playwright, direct HTTP/redirect creation, navigation/reload/history, detach-before-close, and failed-attach rollback pass in both access modes. All six refreshed captures were opened and inspected; source/worker hashes and process/endpoint/temp-state cleanup were verified. This does not claim the operator’s mcporter discovery path or Store deployment was exercised. The public PR screenshots show the byte-identical browser patch before the base refresh; the complete flow was rerun afterward.

The original complete local changed gate passed. On the byte-identical refreshed patch, two repeats passed the preceding guards, export scans, formatting, and both type lanes, then timed out in SDK declaration generation before local lint started (`plugin-sdk boundary root shims timed out after 300000ms`, on Node 26 and Node 24). The successful build did not prevent that repeat. This is a documented local tooling failure; no passing local rerun is claimed and no timeout/skip was introduced. The unchanged declaration tooling and actual completed [hosted extension lint/format job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33223399767/job/99022195062) were inspected. A separate local tooling follow-up is recorded; native preparation will verify the exact-head hosted gates.

The isolated Codex P0/P1 autoreview reported no actionable findings on the exact patch; rebase preserved patch identity and all 19 changed files. The current ClawSweeper review also reports no actionable code/security findings. Both Rank-up moves are addressed by the exact-head CI and direct owner/API/source proof above; no re-review is necessary for an unchanged head reviewed within 12 hours.

Residual limitation accepted within the documented conservative cleanup scope: after handoff, lost acknowledgements or process death can leave a tab. A paused, moved, navigated, replaced, or otherwise taken-over tab is not forcibly reclaimed. No operator Gateway, shared Chrome/mcporter service, live extension configuration, or credentials were changed. No Store release or other publication of a version is part of this landing.
